chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Sinan, from Hudhaifa ibn Mansur, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
The one who is Arabized after migration is the abandoner of this matter after having known it.

key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter (referring to religion, belief, or the Imamate)
key_terms.الْمُعَرَّبُ: The one who is Arabized (adopted Arab customs/identity)
key_terms.الْهِجْرَة: Migration (often referring to the migration of the Prophet or the early community)

ai.seo_question: What does 'Arabization after migration' mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq defining 'al-mu'arrab' not merely as linguistic assimilation, but as a theological state of apostasy where one abandons the 'Amr' (divine authority or belief) after having known it. This definition underscores the Shia emphasis on the necessity of retaining both intellectual conviction and adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt's guidance, linking linguistic identity to spiritual fidelity.
